p: Composed by David concerning the reign of his son Solomon.
judgments: Imbue the king with the Spirit of wisdom and justice, that he reign not as the worldly tyrants do.
son: That is, to his posterity.
mountains shall bring peace to the: When justice reigns, even the places most barren will be enriched with your blessings.
judge the poor of the people: He shows why the sword is committed to Kings that is, to defend the innocent, and suppress the wicked.
fear thee as long as the: The people will embrace your true religion, when you give a king who rules according to your word.
down like rain upon the mown: As this is true in all godly kings, so it is chiefly verified in Christ, who with his heavenly dew, makes his Church ever to flourish.
sea to sea: That is, from the Red sea to the sea called the Syriacum, and from Euphrates forward, meaning, that Christ's kingdom would be large and universal.
Tarshish and of the isles shall: Of Cilicia, and of all other countries beyond the sea, which he means by the isles.
of Sheba and Seba shall offer: That is, of Arabia that rich country, of which Sheba was a part bordering on Ethiopia.
precious shall their blood be in: Though tyrants pause not to shed blood, yet this godly king will preserve his subjects from all kinds of wrong.
gold of Sheba: God will both prosper his life and make the people willing to obey him.
fruit thereof shall shake like Lebanon: Under such a king will be great plenty, both of fruit and also of the increase of mankind.
him blessed: They will pray to God for his continuance and know that God prospers them for his sake.
wondrous things: He confesses that unless God miraculously preserves his people neither the king nor the kingdom can continue.
prayers of David the son of: Concerning his son Solomon.
